component: Chrome V8 (JIT, exploited in the wild)
root_cause: In V8's Ignition bytecode generator the TDZ hole-check elision state (HoleCheckElisionScope) was not scoped to the whole optional chain, so on an optional-chain path that lacked the scope a variable could be recorded as already hole-checked on a short-circuited branch where the check never ran, a later load skipped the hole check, and V8's internal hole value reached script as a wrongly typed object; the fix embeds one HoleCheckElisionScope in OptionalChainNullLabelScope for the entire chain.
notes: Fix commit title: [interpreter] don't elide hole checks across optional chain (review https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/c/v8/v8/+/6678591, main@{#101050}); it only touches OptionalChainNullLabelScope and BuildOptionalChain. VisitDelete as the path that built an optional chain without the elision scope comes from the QiAnXin and retr0.zip analyses, not from the commit. The record labels the component JIT, but the bug is in the Ignition bytecode generator. Shipped in Chrome 138.0.7204.96.

component: Chrome Mojo on Windows (sandbox escape, exploited in the wild)
root_cause: Mojo's ipcz transport on Windows encoded and decoded OS handle values exchanged with a less-trusted process without rejecting Windows pseudo-handle sentinels (Chrome already refused -1, the current-process value, but not -2, the current-thread value, or the other negative sentinels), so a broker that duplicated such a value with DuplicateHandle while relaying a message turned it into a real handle to its own thread; the fix rejects pseudo handles in DecodeHandle and EncodeHandle.
notes: Fix commit title: Avoid receiving or sending sentinel handle values (review https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/c/chromium/src/+/6380193, main@{#1436135}); it also adds base::win::IsPseudoHandle in base/win/win_util.h and PlatformHandle::is_pseudo_handle in mojo/public/cpp/platform/platform_handle.h. DecodeHandle and EncodeHandle are functions in an anonymous namespace in transport.cc. The relay handler ipcz::NodeLink::OnAcceptRelayedMessage is named by Kaspersky; its file in third_party/ipcz was not checked, so a wider audit may add third_party/ipcz. Windows-only code. Fixed in Chrome 134.0.6998.177.

component: Chrome Loader (cross-origin leak, exploited in the wild)
root_cause: Blink's PreloadHelper::LoadLinksFromHeader also processed Link headers carried on subresource responses and honoured their referrerpolicy attribute, so a response from another origin could start a load with a looser Referer policy (such as unsafe-url) than the document's own, sending the full document URL including query parameters; the fix forces no-referrer for Link-header loads that come from subresource responses.
notes: Main commit c3568ced (review https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/c/chromium/src/+/6522070, main@{#1457510}) adds IsSubresourceLoad(mode) and the feature flag kNoReferrerForPreloadFromSubresource; M136 cherry-picks d2f426134c761874afb9b833c2545f925cfe6b40 and 76fa3c17 (minibranch) shipped in 136.0.7103.113. The loader directory is large; the Link header handling in preload_helper.cc is the relevant area.

component: FreeType (font decoding, exploited in the wild)
root_cause: In load_truetype_glyph() the subglyph count of a composite glyph on the TrueType GX / variable font path was stored in a signed short and then used, plus a fixed 4 for phantom points, to size a heap allocation, so a large count wrapped to a tiny buffer that the following point writes overran; FreeType 2.13.1 made the count unsigned and reworked the allocation.
notes: Upstream fixed this in 2.13.1 through refactoring and never marked one commit as the fix. Ubuntu cites ef636696 ([truetype] Clean up zeroing and local variables) and notes the count variable stayed signed there; 73720c7c (load_truetype_glyph: Unsigned fix) changes it to FT_UShort; the Yocto backport uses both. Canonical's oss-security message also points at 47103b2f195e0f9664c9470182f063cb7d41dc9f (phantom point accounting). Commits were read on the GitHub mirror https://github.com/freetype/freetype because GitLab blocked automated reads.

component: Samsung libimagecodec.quram.so (image decoding, zero-click, exploited in the wild)
root_cause: Samsung's closed-source libimagecodec.quram.so image decoder lacked sufficient bounds checks, so a crafted image caused an out-of-bounds write during decoding; the faulty field and code path are not public.
notes: Closed source: question-level test only. Samsung advisory SVE-2025-1702, fixed in SMR Sep-2025 Release 1 (Android 13 and later); reported by Meta and WhatsApp on 2025-08-13; exploited in the wild. Samsung's text only says out-of-bounds write.

component: Windows MSHTML (file association, exploited in the wild)
classes: What is shown versus what is used
root_cause: Windows let an Internet Shortcut (.url) file target the mhtml: protocol handler, which was still registered to the retired Internet Explorer (MSHTML) engine, so opening the shortcut sent the target through IE and its weaker download and HTA handling instead of the default browser, while the file name and icon made it look like a document; the July 2024 update stopped mhtml: from being used this way.
notes: Closed source: question-level test only. Fixed in the July 2024 Windows security update (2024-07-09); Microsoft classes it as an MSHTML platform spoofing vulnerability. Check Point says the fix unregistered mhtml: from Internet Explorer so it opens in Edge. Exploited in the wild (Void Banshee per Trend Micro).

component: Chrome Visuals (use-after-free, exploited in the wild)
classes: Assumptions broken by callbacks and reentrancy
root_cause: FrameSinkBundleImpl::Submit in Chrome's viz service kept raw SinkGroup pointers in local sets while it dispatched each submitted frame, and handling a submission could destroy a SinkGroup, after which the loop still called DidFinishFrame and FlushMessages through the freed pointer; the fix tracks each group with a WeakPtr and skips groups that are gone.
notes: Fix title: Viz: Tolerate SinkGroup destruction during submit (main@{#1298119}, review https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/c/chromium/src/+/5523748); the M124 cherry-pick 072039f0 shipped in 124.0.6367.201. Reachable from a compromised renderer (sandbox escape).

root_cause: Safari holds private TCC entitlements and trusts its per-user configuration files, but the TCC protection of that configuration directory was tied to the user's current home directory path, so after the home directory was changed a process could alter Safari's configuration outside that protection and Safari then used it to reach the camera, microphone and location without a prompt; Apple removed the vulnerable code in macOS Sequoia 15.
notes: Closed source: question-level test only. Record ID is CVE-2024-44133 with the name HM Surf. Fixed in macOS Sequoia 15 (Apple component TCC, resolved by removing the vulnerable code; Apple's impact text mentions MDM-managed devices). Found by Microsoft Threat Intelligence, which saw Adload activity possibly using it.

component: PDF.js (Firefox's built-in viewer and many Electron apps)
root_cause: PDF.js took the FontMatrix array from the PDF font dictionary without checking that its entries are numbers, CompiledFont.compileGlyph put those values into a transform command, and FontFaceObject.getPathGenerator joined the command arguments into JavaScript source compiled with new Function when isEvalSupported was on (the default), so a string entry became code; the fix validates FontMatrix and replaces the eval-based glyph compilation with interpreted drawing operations.
notes: PR #18015 (Simplify the way to pass the glyph drawing instructions from the worker to the main thread) merged as 85e64b5c; its single commit is 551e63901c4e19450673c4832ef2235cf8f2fffa. Released in pdfjs-dist 4.2.67 (last affected 4.1.392); Firefox 126 and ESR 115.11. Workaround: isEvalSupported=false. The sink is in src/display/font_loader.js; the unvalidated FontMatrix read is in src/core/evaluator.js (class PartialEvaluator, method not checked); widen the scope with src/core/font_renderer.js and src/core/evaluator.js to cover the whole data flow.

classes: Multiple representations of the same fact
Consistency across sibling branches and similar entry points
root_cause: PackageInstallerService.createSessionInternal accepted an installer package name without validating its characters, and Settings wrote that name escaped into packages.xml but unescaped into the line- and space-delimited packages.list that run-as parses, so a name with newlines and spaces added fake package entries; the fix drops installer package names that are not valid package names (a follow-up fix in the October 2024 bulletin also checks the second copy of the name that the first fix missed).
notes: Android 12 and 13 only (Meta says Android 14 fixed it by accident). d42af9a5 is the Android 13 backport listed by OSV (cherry-pick of main commit 1f445474, Validate package names passed to the installer, first shipped March 2024); 836750619 (Check whether installerPackageName contains only valid characters) is the October 2024 fix for a bypass of the first patch, branch not checked. The packages.list consumer is system/core run-as via libpackagelistparser. Settings.writePackageListLPr is named by Meta's write-up, not by the fix commits. The pm directory is very large, so the audit scope names the two files.

root_cause: The NodeRestriction admission plugin's admitNode limited what a node may change on its own Node object but did not block changes to ownerReferences, so a node could add an owner reference that made the garbage collector delete its Node object on its behalf (a delete the node may not do directly) and then recreate it with labels and taints the plugin would otherwise reject; the fix forbids any change to ownerReferences on node updates.
notes: 790393ae is the master merge of PR #133467 (single commit 944b0a492356894a24dac5facfe5b9ad7be43b08, do not allow the node to update it's owner reference); backports include release-1.31 PR #133470. Fixed in v1.31.12, v1.32.8 and v1.33.4. Mitigation without upgrading: the OwnerReferencesPermissionEnforcement admission plugin.

root_cause: When kustomize-controller and helm-controller built a client from a tenant-supplied kubeconfig Secret for remote apply, they used the client library's kubeconfig handling unchanged, which runs exec credential plugins and reads file references inside the controller's own process and filesystem; the fix passes the config through fluxcd/pkg runtime/client KubeConfig(), which keeps only inline credentials and copies the exec provider and insecure TLS only when --insecure-kubeconfig-exec or --insecure-kubeconfig-tls is set.
notes: Fix spans three repositories: fluxcd/pkg runtime v0.13.3 (runtime/client/kubeconfig.go, KubeConfig and BindFlags), kustomize-controller PR #593 (merge 55f14b7d, bumps fluxcd/pkg/runtime and applies KubeConfig in clientForKubeConfig) and helm-controller PR #455 (internal/kube/client.go; merge hash not confirmed). Fixed versions differ between sources: the GHSA gives kustomize-controller v0.23.0, helm-controller v0.19.0 and flux2 v0.29.0; the Flux May 2022 blog gives kustomize-controller v0.24.0. Only matters in multi-tenant setups that use kubeconfig secrets for remote clusters.

classes: Consistency across sibling branches and similar entry points
root_cause: pip extracted source distribution tar files with Python's PEP 706 data filter when tarfile had it and otherwise fell back to its own _untar_without_filter code, and that fallback created symbolic links from the archive without checking that their targets stay inside the extraction directory; the fix adds is_symlink_target_in_tar and rejects links that point outside.
notes: f2b92314 is the merge commit of PR #13550; vulnerable_ref is its first parent. Fixed in pip 25.3. Only the fallback used when Python's tarfile lacks PEP 706 filters is affected (the GHSA names 3.9.17, 3.10.12, 3.11.4 and 3.12 as the Python releases that have them).

root_cause: ingress-nginx validated the authtls verify-client annotation with authVerifyClientRegex `on|off|optional|optional_no_ca`, which has no ^ and $ anchors, so any value that merely contained one allowed word passed and the rest of the value, including characters such as carriage returns, was later written into the generated nginx configuration; the fix changes the pattern to `^(on|off|optional|optional_no_ca)$`.
notes: Commit 50f9c83 (Missing anchors in regular expression.) reached main through PR #11717 (merge 1a13bf5c0d7a7b9e26da72d2aa9540073681139e); release-branch cherry-picks are PR #11719 (release-1.11) and PR #11718 (release-1.10). Fixed in controller v1.11.2 and v1.10.4. The ingress-nginx repository has no GitHub advisory; the Kubernetes issue is the official record. authVerifyClientRegex is a package-level variable, not a function.

classes: Consistency across sibling branches and similar entry points
root_cause: Argo CD's project API Server.GetDetailedProject returned the project's repository and cluster objects as loaded, without calling Sanitized() to strip credentials as the other endpoints that return repositories did, so a token with only project get permission received repository and cluster credentials; the fix sanitizes both (adding Cluster.Sanitized()).
notes: Fix commit title: fix(security): repository.GetDetailedProject exposes repo secrets (#24387); it also adds Cluster.Sanitized() in pkg/apis/application/v1alpha1/types.go. Patched in v3.1.2, v3.0.14, v2.14.16 and v2.13.9. The sibling endpoints that already sanitize repositories live in server/repository and server/cluster; widen the scope to server/ if the audit should see that contrast.

classes: Whether declared controls actually take effect
root_cause: Kyverno's cosign matchSignatures skipped the signer identity check whenever subject, issuer and extensions were all empty, and that condition ignored subjectRegExp and issuerRegExp, so a keyless attestor that set only the regex fields accepted a signature from any certificate chaining to the trusted root; the fix adds the regex fields to the condition.
notes: PR #12237 (changes if condition to check for RegExp field) merged 2025-02-28 and was cherry-picked to release-1.13. The GitHub advisory database lists >= 1.13.0, < 1.13.5 as affected and 1.14.0-alpha.1 as patched; the repository advisory text names 1.13.6 and 1.14.0, so check the tag list when choosing a release.

root_cause: Argo CD's default install ran Redis without a password, so any pod that could reach it could rewrite cache entries, and the repo server trusted cached manifests whose only integrity check was a non-cryptographic FNV-64a hash stored with the entry (generateCacheEntryHash); the fix generates an initial Redis password (argocd-redis Secret created by an init container) and passes it to every component in the default manifests.
notes: f1a449e8 is the security merge on the 2.11 line (between v2.11.0 and v2.11.1; 27 files: redis-initial-password admin command, init container, requirepass, REDIS_PASSWORD in every component, HA chart and install manifests). Fixed in 2.11.1, 2.10.10, 2.9.15 and 2.8.19; per-branch commits for the older lines were not collected. The fix commit does not change the FNV-64a entry hash in reposerver/cache/cache.go. The audit scope names two directories because the default-password half and the cache-trust half live in different places.

root_cause: containerd's oci.WithUser parsed a numeric UID:GID with strconv.Atoi and converted the values straight to uint32 without checking that they lie between 0 and math.MaxInt32, so an out-of-range value wrapped around and the container ended up running as root; the fix rejects user and group IDs outside that range.
notes: 1a43cb6a is the release/2.0 security merge (v2.0.4); its commit is a cherry-pick of main commit de1341c2. The advisory lists 05044ec0a9a75232cad458027ca83437aae3f4da for 1.7.27 and cf158e884cfe4812a6c371b59e4ea9bc4c46e51a for 1.6.38; paths there were not checked. Fixed in 2.0.4, 1.7.27 and 1.6.38.

root_cause: Jenkins created its CLI argument parsers (in CLICommand.getCmdLineParser and in CLIRegisterer) with args4j's default ParserProperties, where expandAtFiles is on, so an argument of the form @path was replaced with the contents of that file on the controller before the command saw it; the fix builds the parsers with at-syntax disabled unless the system property hudson.cli.CLICommand.allowAtSyntax is set.
notes: Commit title [SECURITY-3314], included in jenkins-2.442; also fixed in LTS 2.426.3 and 2.440.1 (affected: 2.441 and earlier, LTS 2.426.2 and earlier). The method in CLIRegisterer that builds its CmdLineParser was not confirmed by name, so only the class is listed. The parser default comes from the args4j dependency, not from Jenkins code.

root_cause: To save work, Kyverno skipped policy processing for objects that already had a deletionTimestamp (validationHandler.HandleValidation allowed such UPDATE requests at once, and the mutate-existing and generate paths also skipped them), but a finalizer lets a user keep an object in that state indefinitely while still updating it, so validate, generate and mutate-existing policies, including Enforce ones, were bypassed; the fix removes these deletionTimestamp shortcuts.
notes: The fix spans more than one commit. PR #7039 (fix: remove deletionTimestamp checks, commit 20f74412, in v1.10.0-beta.1) removed the skips in pkg/background/common/resource.go (GetResource) and pkg/webhooks/resource/updaterequest.go (handleMutateExisting). The validate-path skip in pkg/webhooks/resource/validation/validation.go (HandleValidation) is present in v1.9.5 and v1.10.0-alpha.1 but already gone at the parent of PR #7039; the commit that removed it was not identified, so vulnerable_ref and fixed_ref are release tags. At v1.9.5 the skips in validation.go and updaterequest.go were checked directly. pkg/background is outside the audit scope.
